headline: Unconfirmed Houthi strike claims on Riyadh and Yanbu sit against CENTCOM's record Hormuz throughput across a fully halted weekend, with a Monday Nasdaq-100 rebalance waiting beyond the window
body: Every hour published here falls inside the CME weekend halt. Cash equities closed at 20:00Z Friday, the E-mini printed last at 20:59:59Z at 29,917.25 - up 0.59% from a 29,743.00 previous close but 76 points below its 29,993.25 session high, so the final observed futures mark was not a session extreme - and equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z Sunday, two hours after the last slot in this window. No published hour contains a tradable tape. Friday's marks were re-verified at primary sources for this run: the cash Nasdaq-100 settled 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% from a 29,447.00 previous close, finishing 3.63 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range and about 3.6% below its 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. VIX settled 14.81, down 4.08% from 15.44, at the low of a 14.80-15.63 range. The Fed H.15 release shows the 10-year at 4.94% and the 2-year at 4.67% for 17 September, both easing from 5.01% and 4.74% on 16 September, while the effective federal funds rate stepped to 3.88% from 3.63% after the FOMC raised the target range to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September in a unanimous 12-0 vote. WTI settled 100.30, down 1.58%, and Brent 103.87, down 0.91%, a third consecutive decline. The geopolitical file remains two-sided and unresolved. On Saturday the Houthis claimed missile and drone attacks on sensitive sites in Riyadh, where a large plume of black smoke rose from the fuel storage area at King Khalid International Airport, and on an Aramco facility at Yanbu on the Red Sea; the group described the operation as retaliation for an alleged attack on Sanaa. The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed a missile aimed at Riyadh and foiled attacks on Bish, Farasan, Taif and Yanbu, but there has been no Saudi confirmation that any claimed target was struck. Running directly against that, CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper said in a Saturday video message that oil and gas transits through the Strait of Hormuz have reached a six-month high, with U.S. forces helping move more than one billion barrels out of the Persian Gulf over roughly two months. Crude had already fallen for three sessions into Friday. One further verified item is index-specific rather than geopolitical: the Nasdaq-100 quarterly rebalance takes effect Monday and confirms SpaceX at 2.82% of the index, up from roughly 1.28%, calculated on Friday's closing prices, which obliges the more than 200 tracking products holding over $800 billion of assets to adjust. That is a Monday-open mechanical flow and falls entirely outside this window. Because the venue is shut throughout, Tail holds near its structural floor - there is no mechanism by which mean reversion can fail inside a halted market. Tail eases to 4 through the deepest part of the halt, returns to 5 from 05:00Z Sunday, steps to 6 from 10:00Z, 7 from 14:00Z, 8 from 17:00Z and reaches a window high of 9 in the final slot, reflecting accumulating untested headline exposure ahead of an unpriced reopen rather than any observed structure. Stress traces the same shape from a low of 22 to a high of 30, crossing into the moderate band from 10:00Z Sunday. Confidence is solid rather than high: the evidence set is complete and primary-source verified, but it is static, and Friday's marks age through every subsequent hour with no tape able to refresh them. The shared cross-asset context file was read for this run and was more than 90 minutes old, with its futures and calendar sections reported unavailable, so it was treated as stale and the assessment rests on independent primary-source research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail entered the window at 11 as Friday's triple-witching session closed, fell through 7 and 6 as the contract settled, and then held 5 across the final twenty-one slots. Stress began at 33, decayed through 28, 27, 26, 25 and 24 into the halt, bottomed at 21 for five consecutive hours, and edged back to 24 across the last four slots. Dominant mode was normal in all 24 hours, because no venue was open to produce classifiable structure after the first slot. Confidence started at 87 and declined steadily to 73 as the live tape gave way to the weekend and Friday's marks aged. No hour in the lookback is unavailable.
outlookSummary: All 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt: cash closed 20:00Z Friday, the E-mini printed last at 20:59:59Z, and CME equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z Sunday, two hours after the final slot here. No published hour contains a tradable tape, and no scheduled U.S. macro release falls inside the window - the next U.S. catalyst is the Goolsbee speech at 10:30Z Monday, and the first high-impact releases are Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs. Tail holds 5 for one hour, eases to 4 through the deepest part of the halt, returns to 5 from 05:00Z Sunday, steps to 6 from 10:00Z, 7 from 14:00Z and 8 from 17:00Z, and prints a window high of 9 in the final 20:00Z slot as untested weekend headline exposure accumulates toward an unpriced reopen. Stress mirrors that shape between a low of 22 and a high of 30, crossing into the moderate band from 10:00Z Sunday. Confidence declines gently from 72 to 64 as Friday's verified marks age. Every step is a function of venue distance and accumulating unpriced information rather than observed price structure, and dominant mode stays normal throughout because a halted venue has no structure to classify. Tail is capped in single digits because the weekend evidence remains genuinely two-sided: unconfirmed strike claims on Riyadh and Yanbu argue one way, while CENTCOM's six-month-high Hormuz throughput statement, the absence of any Saudi confirmation of damage and three straight sessions of crude decline argue the other. Monday's Nasdaq-100 rebalance flow is a documented checkpoint for the new week but falls outside this publication.
